title: Submit your first job
story: run_mpnn.sh is a job script: the #SBATCH lines at the top ask for a GPU, and the rest runs ProteinMPNN. Hand it to Slurm, then look at the queue.

lesson.title: Reading a job script's #SBATCH lines
lesson.intro: A job script asks for its resources in `#SBATCH` lines at the top. They're the same options you'd give `srun`.

parts.note: The queue. `gpu` allows up to 2 days.
Stop after 2 hours, finished or not.
Save printed output here. `%j` becomes the job ID.

lesson.why: `sbatch` queues the script and gives you your prompt back. The job runs when the GPU is free, even after you log out.

files.~/{{project}}/run_mpnn.sh:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=mpnn
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --output=slurm-%j.out

module load anaconda
conda activate proteinmpnn

python /opt/ProteinMPNN/protein_mpnn_run.py \
  --pdb_path inputs/target.pdb \
  --out_folder outputs/

tasks.text: Look at your jobs in the queue

hints: Run `sbatch run_mpnn.sh`, then `squeue --me`. ST says PD (waiting) or R (running).
